value: response to brown snake scent differed significantly from the water control (P = 0.005) and the novel control (P = 0.022)
method: behavioural: tongue flicks at scented paper towels in the enclosure, PERMANOVA pair-wise tests
conditions: 57 pygmy bluetongue lizards in three groups: 20 wild lizards tested in the field at their natural burrows at Tiliqua Reserve, about 10 km from Burra, and, at Monarto Safari Park, 9 wild-born captive adults (potentially predator-experienced) and 28 captive-born predator-naive offspring housed individually with artificial burrows; scent = paper towel left 48 h in a reptile enclosure, frozen at -20 C and used within 3 weeks, pinned about 5 cm from the lizard's burrow; each lizard met each of five scents once over a 5-day period, order randomised; 30 min acclimation after camera setup then 30 min filmed, tongue flicks at the scent paper counted; scents: eastern brown snake (one animal), eastern bluetongue lizard and Rosenberg's monitor (probably pooled from several animals), a novel control (1:10 diluted eucalyptus oil) and distilled water; mean tongue flicks brown snake 24.07 ± 4.93 s.e., bluetongue 14.33 ± 2.83, monitor 12.81 ± 4.04, novel control 5.81 ± 1.73, water 5.42 ± 1.59; no significant difference among the other treatments, so only the snake scent differed from the controls; tongue flicks did not differ significantly among lizard origins or days; temperature (16.8 to 30.1 C, covariate) had a significant effect on tongue flicks; basking time did not differ with treatment; repeated-measures PERMANOVA; no scent dose and no health screening reported

source.authors: Daniell TL, Hutchinson MN, Ainsley P, Gardner MG
source.title: Recognition of reptile predator scent is innate in an endangered lizard species

where: Results, Differential response to scent treatments
quote: Response to the brown snake treatment differed significantly from both the water control (PERMANOVA pair-wise test P = 0.005) and novel control (PERMANOVA pair-wise test P = 0.022).
note: The sentence says response; the response counted was tongue flicks. Authors read the result as innate recognition of a predator by scent. value: significant between-group main effect for larvae distribution with a bullfrog visible versus no bullfrog (GEE beta = 0.164, p = 0.011)
method: behavioural: spatial distribution of larvae (generalized estimating equation model) with a visible predator behind a clear panel
conditions: Larvae hatched in the lab from eggs collected in the Chinhai Spiny Newt Nature Conservation Area in April-May 2024 and reared without predator exposure; larval stage not stated; 30 replicates, each of five larvae run first as their own control (empty side compartments with water at the same depth) and then, the same five larvae retained, with one American bullfrog (large class, 258.26 ± 19.70 g) placed at random in a side compartment, so control always preceded the cue; 60 x 30 x 10 cm acrylic tank, water 4.5 cm deep, three compartments separated by high-transparency acrylic panels, leak-checked for 48 h to exclude chemical cues; 5 min acclimation then larvae in the distal zone counted at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 min; the group-by-time interaction was significant at 4 and 6 min, and the text and Table 2 give different values for 4 min (beta 0.182, p 0.018 against 0.233, p 0.004); the visual cue also lowered midline crossings (4.167 ± 2.718 against 5.333 ± 2.551, Wilcoxon signed-rank V = 288, p = 0.017)

source.authors: Feng S, Li W, An D, Ma Z, Luo Z, Xu A

quote: Based on the results of the Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) model (Table 2), the between-group main effect was significant (β = 0.164, Wald χ2 = 6.416, p = 0.011).
note: Larvae of an endangered newt responded to a bullfrog it has not co-evolved with. The sentence states the effect size; the paper's wording is that visual cues alone produced quick avoidance and lower activity.

value: larval midline crossings with bullfrog odour water 3.167 +/- 1.555, significantly lower than control 5.500 +/- 2.240
units: midline crossings by the five larvae together in 10 min
method: behavioural: midline crossings in 10 min after injecting bullfrog-conditioned water into a side compartment
conditions: Chemical cue = 30 mL of water conditioned 24 h by four adult bullfrogs fed frog tadpoles (1 L sun-exposed water, filtered), injected into one side compartment behind perforated acrylic partitions (2 mm pores); 30 replicates, each of five lab-hatched, predator-naive larvae (stage not stated) run first as their own control (30 mL plain sun-exposed water) and then, the same five retained, with the cue, so control always preceded the cue; Wilcoxon signed-rank V = 314, p < 0.001; odour concentration not given beyond the volume; whether ± is SD or SE not stated in the passage read; the same cue produced no significant overall spatial avoidance (see the companion record)

source.authors: Feng S, Li W, An D, Ma Z, Luo Z, Xu A

quote: In the experimental group, the total number of midline crossings by larvae within 10 min was 3.167 ± 1.555 times, which was significantly lower than that in the control group (5.500 ± 2.240 times).
note: Activity reduction to a chemical cue; no avoidance was found.

value: no significant main effect of group on larval spatial distribution with bullfrog odour water (GEE beta = 0.188, p = 0.205)
method: behavioural: spatial distribution of larvae (generalized estimating equation model) after bullfrog-conditioned water was added to one side compartment
conditions: Null result for avoidance by odour alone; the group-by-time interaction was significant only at 6 min (beta = -0.302, p = 0.042); 30 replicates, each of five lab-hatched, predator-naive larvae run first as their own control (30 mL plain water) and then, the same five retained, with 30 mL of water conditioned 24 h by four adult bullfrogs, so control always preceded the cue; bullfrog odour dose beyond volume not given; the same cue lowered activity (see the companion record)
